correctness.rationale: The quoted wild number equals k_red+k_blue-2 by contracting monochromatic components and using disjoint opposite-colour quotient spanning trees. Graphic rank subadditivity gives lower L; explicit K_{3,4} two complementary spanning trees and arbitrary-part extension attain zero; a=2 and K3,3 have separate constructions. Every pair of differently coloured edges lies on a K_{a,b} four-cycle; the mixed-cycle rank argument yields r_red+r_blue>=a+b, hence upper a+b-2. One isolated-colour edge attains it. Surjective-colouring subset graph is connected by one-edge recolourings and each move changes the wild number by at most one, filling the entire interval. All arguments respect a,b>=2 and surjectivity. Exhaustive independent union-find spectra K22,K23,K24,K33,K34,K35 reproduced every integer between claimed endpoints.
residual_risks: The exact interval proof, not finite graph enumeration, establishes all sizes; surjectivity and a>=2 are essential.

value.rationale: The unrestricted surjective colourings of K_{a,b} form a standard natural finite graph family. Determining the entire sharp integer spectrum, with two thin exceptional regimes and no internal gaps, is a structural classification useful when comparing constrained variants; it is not a restatement of the known component formula.
residual_risks: Counts per value, >=3 colours, and balanced/proper restrictions are not classified.

final_claim: For every integers 2<=a<=b, the wild-number spectrum of unrestricted surjective two-edge-colourings of K_{a,b} is every integer from L=max(0,2(a+b-1)-ab) through a+b-2; in particular L=2 if a=2, L=1 if a=b=3, otherwise zero.
limitations: No equitable/proper-colouring spectrum is asserted and no frequency counts are obtained.
